meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

examples.trans: The order is completely backward! Since when does an add-on go ahead of the main star?
The topic of order, billing sequence came up in today's meeting.

examples.text: 인사도 예쁘게 한다! 이래서 머리 검은 짐승은 거두는 게 아니라고 어른들 말 틀린 거 하나도 없어!
examples.trans: What a sweet farewell—and just a card?! The elders were right: never take in a human stray!

examples.text: 순서가 틀렸잖아요! 옵션이 앞에 가는 경우가 어딨어?
examples.trans: The order is completely backward! Since when does an add-on go ahead of the main star?

Go forward.
Do well in the future.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

examples.text: 뭔 이런 경우가 다 있냐? 나는 피디가 출연자 밀어서 입원시킨 것도 처음이지만 이렇게 항의 전화 많이 받아보는 것도 처음이다.
examples.trans: What kind of mess is this? Seeing a producer hospitalize a cast member is a first for me, and getting this many protest calls over an article is a first too.
This point about situation, case is really important.
Where is my handbag?

examples.text: 글쎄 그게 무슨 또라이 같은 소리냐고! 박 군은 어딨니?
examples.trans: What kind of lunatic excuse is that?! Where is Manager Park?

examples.text: 의자, 내 앞에 놓으면 어떡해? 거울 앞에 놔야지.
examples.trans: That chair—why put it in front of me? Put it in front of the mirror.
The topic of chair came up in today's meeting.
This is my bag.
My younger sibling is a student.

놓다.gloss: to put, to place, to leave

meanings.en: to put, to place, to leave
meanings.note: Often used as an auxiliary verb to indicate leaving something in a certain state.

examples.trans: Please place it on the desk.
I left the door open.

meanings.en: what to do, how to act

examples.trans: What should we do?
What should we do? (2)

examples.text: 보고 나서 느낀 점은 신디 씨는 메인 카메라가 돌지 않거나 거울을 보고 있지 않을 때 훨씬 더 예쁘다는 겁니다, 지금처럼.
examples.trans: What I realized afterward is that you look far prettier when the main camera is not rolling and you are not looking in a mirror—like right now.

examples.text: 의자, 내 앞에 놓으면 어떡해? 거울 앞에 놔야지.
examples.trans: That chair—why put it in front of me? Put it in front of the mirror.

Where are you going?

examples.trans: Why are you running?

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this

examples.text: 야, 너 초딩이냐? 유치해서 웃음도 안 나와.
examples.trans: Hey, are you a grade-schooler? That is so childish I cannot even laugh.
It is really because it is childish compared to what I expected.
Do you tend to stay out overnight pretty often?

I went to the market with my mum.
The food my mum makes is the most delicious.

examples.text: 그냥 내버려 둬, 쟤 완전 취했어.
examples.trans: Just leave him alone, he is completely wasted.

Please sit on the chair.
I sat on the floor.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.

meanings.note: Used for phones, alarms, or bells ringing. With -면 (울리면), it means 'if it rings'. RR: ullida.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Humble 1st person plural pronoun used when speaking to superiors or in formal settings.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

examples.text: 예, 실장님 연락처 받았습니다. 공항 도착하는 대로 바로 연락드리겠습니다.
examples.trans: Yes, Director, I got the contact info. I will call you the moment we arrive at the airport.

examples.text: 아니 근데 저희 대표님이 설마 그러시겠어요? 혹시 그런 일 생기면 연락드릴게요, 명함 주세요.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
